Source: parent Step 4, '(∗) holds for Lipschitz v: with v_δ := v ∗ φ_δ (componentwise mollification), ... Dv_δ = (Dv) ∗ φ_δ'; this child is the identity Dv_δ = (Dv) ∗ φ_δ for one component and an arbitrary C¹ compactly supported kernel. It combines Mathlib's differentiation of convolutions with the integration-by-parts formula for Lipschitz functions (Mathlib LipschitzWith.integral_lineDeriv_mul_eq, the tool named in the parent's (M_1) step).

Notation: λ = Lebesgue measure (volume) on ℝᵏ = Euclid k; D = fderiv ℝ; ∂_w F(s) := lineDeriv ℝ F s w, the derivative of t ↦ F(s + t·w) at t = 0 (0 if it does not exist).

1. (Convolution.) f_ρ(y) = ∫ ρ(t)·f(y − t) dt is the convolution ρ ⋆ f with the multiplication pairing (Mathlib convolution ρ f (lsmul ℝ ℝ) λ, convolution_def).
2. (Differentiation under the integral.) ρ is C¹ with compact support and f is continuous (being Lipschitz), hence locally integrable. Therefore ρ ⋆ f is differentiable at x with derivative (Dρ ⋆ f)(x) = ∫ f(x − t)·Dρ(t) dt, a Bochner integral of continuous linear maps (Mathlib HasCompactSupport.hasFDerivAt_convolution_left). Its integrand is integrable because Dρ is continuous with compact support and f is continuous (HasCompactSupport.convolutionExists_left). Evaluation at v is continuous linear and commutes with the Bochner integral (ContinuousLinearMap.integral_apply), so Df_ρ(x)v = ∫ Dρ(t)v·f(x − t) dt.
3. (Change of variables.) λ is invariant under s ↦ x − s (integral_sub_left_eq_self), so ∫ Dρ(t)v·f(x − t) dt = ∫ Dρ(x − s)v·f(s) ds and ∫ ρ(t)·Df(x − t)v dt = ∫ ρ(x − s)·Df(s)v ds. It remains to show ∫ Dρ(x − s)v·f(s) ds = ∫ ρ(x − s)·Df(s)v ds.
4. (Reflected kernel.) Let h(s) := ρ(x − s). h is C¹ (ρ composed with an affine map) and has compact support (its support is the image of the support of ρ under the homeomorphism s ↦ x − s); a C¹ function with compact support is Lipschitz (ContDiff.lipschitzWith_of_hasCompactSupport). By the chain rule Dh(s) = −Dρ(x − s), so ∂_{−v}h(s) = Dh(s)(−v) = Dρ(x − s)v for every s.
5. (Integration by parts for Lipschitz functions.) For the L-Lipschitz f and the Lipschitz, compactly supported h, LipschitzWith.integral_lineDeriv_mul_eq gives ∫ ∂_v f(s)·h(s) ds = ∫ ∂_{−v}h(s)·f(s) ds. By step 4 the right side equals ∫ Dρ(x − s)v·f(s) ds.
6. (Rademacher.) f is differentiable at λ-a.e. s (LipschitzWith.ae_differentiableAt), and at such s, ∂_v f(s) = Df(s)v (DifferentiableAt.lineDeriv_eq_fderiv). Hence ∫ ∂_v f(s)·h(s) ds = ∫ ρ(x − s)·Df(s)v ds (integral_congr_ae).
7. (Conclusion.) Steps 5 and 6 give ∫ Dρ(x − s)v·f(s) ds = ∫ ρ(x − s)·Df(s)v ds, which by steps 2 and 3 is Df_ρ(x)v = ∫ ρ(t)·Df(x − t)v dt.
